items.summary: Recent advances in video generation call for reliable detection grounded in explicit forensic evidence. items.summary: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. items.title: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
items.summary: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce WeMM-Video, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. items.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. items.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
items.summary: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. items.summary: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. items.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables object-level operations on Gaussian primitives, yet existing segmentation methods are largely trained and evaluated through rendered views. items.summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. items.title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
items.summary: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. items.title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
items.summary: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. items.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. To support such decisions, the Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test) was introduced for dense settings where all items are annotated by the same annotators. items.title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
items.summary: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? items.summary: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. items.summary: Mixture of Block Attention (MoBA) reduces long-context computation by selecting key-value (KV) blocks for each query. FlashMoBA implements MoBA efficiently but retains a fixed Top-k budget and query-centric schedule. items.title: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. items.summary: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. items.title: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
items.summary: World models aim to predict environment dynamics under actions, enabling the prediction of action consequences without executing them in the real world. items.title: WM^MLLM: Turning MLLMs into World Models
items.summary: Video world models keep the world in the context of a generator, so a revisit is synthesized again and earlier edits can drift or disappear. We present WM^MLLM, the first interactive world model built on multimodal large language models (MLLMs), for persistent, editable world generation from a single image. items.summary: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. items.summary: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. items.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
items.summary: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends.
